locale.name: package.description
locale.en: This package contains bricks for presenting apps or programs on your website.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.description
locale.en:
This brick places two images exactly on top of each other and lets visitors fade between "before" and "after" using a draggable handle. It makes changes immediately tangible – ideal for renovation, retouching, refurbishment or product comparison.

  • Intuitive to use: Drag with mouse and touch, click to jump, fine-tune with the keyboard – on desktop and mobile alike.
  • Eye-catcher on scroll: A subtle intro animation hints, as it becomes visible, that the slider can be moved.
  • Fits your design: Orientation, handle and label style, color scheme (brand color, white or black) and rounded corners are configurable.
  • Accessible: keyboard operable and exposed to screen readers.

That lets you illustrate the difference between two states with a single brick – directly in the editor, without writing a line of code.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.labelMode.desc
locale.en: Controls this side's label: "Default text" shows the standard output used in the frontend, "Custom text" reveals a field for your own label, "Hide" shows no label.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.labelPosition.desc
locale.en: Sets where the labels sit: top, center or bottom (for vertical orientation accordingly left, center or right).

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.labelStyle.desc
locale.en: Visual style of the label: "Box" (light, semi-transparent background with dark text), "Pill" (dark, strongly rounded background with white text) or "Text only" with a subtle shadow.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.handleStyle.desc
locale.en: Appearance of the handle on the dividing line: "Circle with arrows" or a plain line with a small grip in the center.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.orientation.desc
locale.en: Direction of the dividing line and the swipe: "Horizontal" fades from left to right, "Vertical" from top to bottom.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.startPosition.desc
locale.en: Initial handle position in percent (0–100): 0 initially shows only the "after" image, 100 only "before", 50 splits the image in the middle.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.aspectRatio.desc
locale.en: Aspect ratio of the comparison area. "Automatic" adopts the ratio of the "after" image; fixed values (16:9, 4:3, 1:1) enforce the format and crop the images centered (object-fit: cover). For a clean result, upload both images at the same size.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.maxWidth.desc
locale.en: Limits the width of the comparison area and centers it. Leave empty for full width (100%). CSS length such as 600px, 80% or 40rem; a plain number is treated as pixels.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.handleColor.desc
locale.en: Color scheme for the dividing line and handle. "Brand color" uses the project's primary color, "White" and "Black" are neutral variants with slight transparency. The icon inside the handle uses the matching contrast color.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.introAnimation.desc
locale.en: When enabled, the handle briefly moves left and right and back to the start position when the brick first becomes visible – a subtle hint that the slider is interactive. Enabled by default.

locale.name: control.ImageCompare.borderRadius.desc
locale.en: Rounds the corners of the image area. Enabled by default.

locale.en: Text on a background image with an arrow that scrolls to the next section.

locale.name: control.WallpaperText.description
locale.en: With this brick you can quickly create a banner. Choose a suitable image or color to be displayed below the text.

locale.name: control.WallpaperText.minHeight.desc
locale.en: Please enter the value with a valid CSS unit (e.g. 500px, 80vh, etc.)

locale.name: control.WallpaperText.imageLoading.desc
locale.en: Use “Deferred” only for bricks below the visible area. Keep “Eager” for hero or top-of-page bricks.

locale.name: control.WallpaperText.borderRadius.desc
locale.en: Rounds the brick's corners. Whether and how strongly the corners are rounded depends on the active template – not every template supports rounded corners. For full-width bricks, we recommend disabling this option.

locale.name: control.WallpaperText.fontColor.desc
locale.en: For darker background you can change the default content color here. Please note that depending on the template, the titles (h1, h2, etc.) may have the color set separately.

locale.name: control.counter.description
locale.en:
Use this brick to present key figures, statistics or milestones as animated counters. Each entry supports its own start and end value and can count up or down automatically. The presentation can be varied to match your content and layout.
  • Layout: inline left, inline centered, stacked left, stacked centered or horizontal
  • Duration: animation duration for all counters in milliseconds
  • Start at 0: ignores individual start values and always begins at zero
  • Icon on top: displays the entry icon above the counter value
  • Entries: any number of values with prefix, suffix, title, text and optional icon

locale.name: brick.setting.counter.duration.desc
locale.en: Duration of the count animation in milliseconds. Default: 2500.

locale.name: brick.setting.counter.maxWidth.desc
locale.en: Limits the width of the entire counter brick or its entry area. Any CSS unit, e.g. 900px, 60rem, 100%. A bare number is interpreted as pixels. Empty = no limit.

locale.name: brick.setting.counter.itemMaxWidth.desc
locale.en: Limits the width of individual counter entries. Examples: 18rem, 22rem, 320px, 28ch. A bare number is interpreted as pixels. Empty = no limit.

locale.name: brick.counter.entries.endValue.desc
locale.en: Target value of the counter. If the end value is lower than the start value, the counter counts down.

locale.name: brick.counter.entries.prefix.desc
locale.en: Text directly before the counter. In many templates it is smaller than the number. Examples: + before 100 results in +100, about before 250 results in about 250.

locale.name: brick.counter.entries.numberAddon.desc
locale.en: Short addon placed directly next to the number. Useful for abbreviations like k, M or mn. Example: 10 with addon k becomes 10k. If you want a spelling with a space, include it in the addon itself, for example M for 2.5 M. Use the suffix field for trailing characters with their own spacing such as + or %.

locale.name: brick.counter.entries.suffix.desc
locale.en: Text directly after the counter. In many templates it is smaller than the number. Examples: years after 15 results in 15 years, % after 80 results in 80%.

locale.name: brick.counter.entries.title.desc
locale.en: Small heading for the counter. It is displayed below or next to the number and is smaller than the value.

locale.name: brick.counter.entries.content.desc
locale.en: Optional short explanatory text for the counter. It is displayed smaller and more subtly than title and number.

locale.name: brick.counter.entries.delete.title
locale.en: Do you really want to remove this counter entry?

locale.name: brick.counter.entries.delete.text
locale.en: Do you really want to remove this counter entry?

locale.name: brick.counter.entries.delete.information
locale.en: The counter entries can not be restored.

locale.name: control.progressbar.description
locale.en:
Use this brick to present progress, values or proportions clearly with bars. It is suitable for skills, project status, workloads or key figures. The presentation can be adjusted flexibly to match your content, layout and visual style.
  • Any number of entries with title and percentage value
  • Optional custom color for each bar
  • Additional text area above, below, left or right of the bars
  • Separate text position for mobile view
  • Different bar layouts: default, wide or overlay with text inside the bar
  • Animation can be disabled, triggered once on scroll into view or linked to scrolling
  • Maximum width for bars and the complete layout area can be configured

locale.name: brick.setting.progressbar.maxWidth.desc
locale.en: Any CSS unit, e.g. 600px, 40rem, 80%. A bare number is interpreted as pixels. Empty = no limit.

locale.name: brick.setting.progressbar.containerMaxWidth.desc
locale.en: Limits the width of the whole layout area (text + bars). The brick's header and content stay untouched. Any CSS unit, empty = full width.

locale.name: brick.setting.progressbar.additionalText.desc
locale.en: The text can be shown above, below, left or right of the bars. It does not replace the brick's regular content. When additional text is set, the settings additional text position, column distribution and vertical alignment become relevant.

locale.name: brick.setting.progressbar.textColumnWidth.desc
locale.en: Ratio between text column and bars column. Only applies when text position is set to left or right.

locale.name: brick.setting.progressbar.verticalAlign.desc
locale.en: Vertical alignment of text and bars relative to each other. Only applies when text position is set to left or right.

locale.name: brick.setting.progressbar.mobileTextPosition.desc
locale.en: On narrow screens (container narrower than 45rem) the layout always becomes single-column. Choose whether the text appears above or below the bars.

locale.name: brick.setting.progressbar.barLayout.desc
locale.en: Visual variant of the bars. Default: thin bar with label above. Wide: thicker bar. Overlay: label sits directly on the bar.

locale.name: brick.setting.progressbar.barLayout.overlay
locale.en: Overlay - text on top of the bar

locale.name: brick.setting.progressbar.animation.desc
locale.en: None: bars are shown filled immediately. Once when scrolled into view: bars fill once as soon as the brick enters the viewport. Scroll-driven: fill follows the scroll position (modern browsers only; falls back to fully filled). Animation is disabled when the user has set "reduce motion".

locale.name: brick.progressbar.entries.delete.title
locale.en: Do you really want to remove this progressbar entry?

locale.name: brick.progressbar.entries.delete.text
locale.en: Do you really want to remove this progressbar entry?

locale.name: brick.progressbar.entries.delete.information
locale.en: The progressbar entries can not be restored

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.poster.desc
locale.en: This is an image to be shown while the video is downloading, or until the user hits the play button.

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.borderRadius.desc
locale.en: Rounds the brick's corners. Whether and how strongly the corners are rounded depends on the active template – not every template supports rounded corners. For full-width bricks, we recommend disabling this option.

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.imageLoading.desc
locale.en: Use “Deferred” only when the brick is below the visible area. Keep “Eager” for hero or top-of-page bricks.

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.shortVideo.desc
locale.en: If selected, this video will be loaded as background video. You can open the uncut version in popup (see more settings below).

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.lazyLoadMode.desc
locale.en: By default, the video is only built after the page has fully loaded. A poster should be set for this. Without a poster, the video will still load immediately.

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.lazyLoadMode.afterWindowLoad
locale.en: Load only after full page load

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.autoplay.desc
locale.en: The video automatically begins to play back as soon as it can do so without stopping to finish loading the data. In some browsers (e.g. Chrome 70.0) autoplay doesn't work if muted option is not active.

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.muted.desc
locale.en: The audio will be initially silenced.

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.loop.desc
locale.en: If active, the browser will automatically seek back to the start upon reaching the end of the video

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.playsinline.desc
locale.en: If activated the video is to be played "inline", that is within the element's playback area. Note that the absence of this attribute does not imply that the video will always be played in fullscreen. Read more at What Does `playsinline` Mean in Web Video?.

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.playIfInView.desc
locale.en: The video will only play if it is in the visible area, otherwise the video will be paused, e.g. when the user scrolls further on the page.

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.backgroundVideoBrightness.desc
locale.en: To make the text above the background video more visible, you can darken the video with this option. Please enter value between 0 and 100.

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.openVideoInPopup.desc
locale.en: This option is useful when a shortened video is played in the background. The user can watch the full video in a popup. You can use either the built-in button or your own button. The built-in button is displayed below the content. If you want to use your own button, you need to set the attribute data-js="openVideoInPopupBtn" on it

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.openVideoInPopup.clickOnDefaultButton
locale.en: Click on the default button opens a popup with video

locale.name: control.backgroundVideo.openVideoInPopup.clickOnOwnButton
locale.en: Click on own button opens popup with video

locale.name: control.video.videoButtonAction.playInWebsite

locale.name: control.video.maxVideoWidth.desc

locale.name: control.video.maxContentWidth.desc

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.description
locale.en:
With this brick a section stays in place while scrolling and moves large cards smoothly sideways across the screen. A plain list turns into a small staging – ideal for services, process steps, product benefits or references.

  • Motion that matches the scroll: The cards follow the scroll progress exactly instead of running their own animation – no stutter, no overshoot.
  • Cards with substance: Per card an image, text or both side by side, plus an overline, automatic numbering, an icon and a button that makes the whole card clickable.
  • Live counter: Shows "01 / 03" – built in at the top right, hidden, or at a position of your choice inside the content.
  • Usable everywhere: On touch devices, in narrow windows, without JavaScript and with reduced motion the very same cards simply appear below each other.

This gives a page a real eye-catcher without visitors on small devices or with accessibility settings missing anything.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.entries.desc
locale.en: The cards of the section, in the order they are moved through. From two cards on the desktop scroll takes over, below that the cards appear below each other. All cards are as tall as the tallest one – so keep the content per card similar in length and short enough to fit on the screen.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.cardWidth.desc
locale.en: Width of the active, centered card – relative to the page content width, not to the screen. The narrower the card, the more of the previous and the next card is visible.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.speed.desc
locale.en: How much scroll distance is spent on one card. "Slow" keeps the section pinned longer and leaves more time to read, "fast" moves the cards through more briskly. The total length follows automatically from the number of cards.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.contentVerticalAlign
locale.en: Vertical alignment of the text areas

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.contentVerticalAlign.desc
locale.en: Every card is as tall as the longest one. This setting decides where a shorter text sits inside that height. Applies to all cards and to both text areas, so the rhythm stays the same across the cards. Whenever a text is taller than the screen it always starts at the top, so that nothing slips past the upper edge.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.showNumbers.desc
locale.en: Shows a running number (01, 02, 03 …) on every card. The number follows automatically from the card order and does not have to be maintained.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.counterMode.desc
locale.en: The counter ("01 / 03") shows which card is currently visible. It only appears while the section is actually pinned – in the stacked presentation it is hidden.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.counterMode.inline
locale.en: Built in, top right next to the content

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.counterTarget.desc
locale.en: Place an empty placeholder in the content of this brick, for example <div data-name="cardCounter"></div>, and enter exactly that name here (so cardCounter). The counter is then moved into it. If the placeholder is not found, the counter stays at its built in position at the top right.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.delete.information
locale.en: The selected card is removed from the section. This can only be undone by cancelling the brick editing.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.active.desc
locale.en: An inactive card stays stored, but is not rendered and not counted.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.layout.desc
locale.en: Decides which areas the card uses. In the split variants the two areas sit side by side on the desktop; as soon as the cards appear below each other, the areas do too - with an image that means: image on top.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.splitRatio.desc
locale.en: Width ratio of the left to the right column, for example "60 / 40" = left column 60 %, right column 40 %. Only applies to the split layouts.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.image.desc
locale.en: The image of the card. It fills its column completely, so pick a motif that tolerates being cropped at the edges.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.cardIcon.desc
locale.en: Small symbol above the heading. Either a FontAwesome class (for example "fa-solid fa-rocket") – the usual way – or alternatively an image from the media manager.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.eyebrow.desc
locale.en: Short line above the heading that classifies the card – for example "Step 1" or "Consulting". Rendered in the overline style of the template.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.title.desc
locale.en: The heading of the card. It is also used as the alternative text of the card image.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.contentPrimary.desc
locale.en: Body text of the card. Keep it short: the scroll effect needs cards that fit on the screen completely. If the tallest card no longer fits, the section shows the cards below each other instead of cutting content off.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.buttonText.desc
locale.en: Label of the button. If the field stays empty and a target is set, "Learn more" is used.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.link.desc
locale.en: Internal page or external address. Without a target no button is shown. With a target the whole card becomes clickable as well.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.linkNofollow.desc
locale.en: Tells search engines not to follow the link. Useful for paid or third party targets, not needed for normal internal links.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.btnType.desc
locale.en: Colour variant of the button from the design system of the template – the same selection as in the button brick. "primary" is the main action.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.buttonSize.desc
locale.en: Applies to the buttons of all cards, so the section stays consistent.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.imageMaxHeight.desc
locale.en: Limits the height of the image for this card only, for example "320" for 320 pixels. A number without a unit is read as pixels, values like "50vh" or "20rem" work as well. Leave empty to use the global setting of the brick.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.imageFit.desc
locale.en: Defines how the image fills its space. "Fill the area" always covers the space completely and crops the edges – good for photos. "Show completely" scales the image down until all of it is visible and leaves empty space – good for logos, screenshots or graphics where nothing may be missing. With "Use the global setting" whatever is configured on the brick applies.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.imageCrop.desc
locale.en: Which part of the image always stays visible when it gets cropped. Example: for a portrait choose "Top" so the head is not cut off. Only has an effect together with "Fill the area". With "Use the global setting" whatever is configured on the brick applies.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.buttonIcon.desc
locale.en: FontAwesome class for a small symbol inside the button, for example "fa-solid fa-arrow-right". Leave empty for a button without a symbol. Not to be confused with the card icon further above.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.buttonIconPosition.desc
locale.en: Whether the symbol sits before or after the label. Arrows usually go after the text, explanatory symbols before it.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.buttonClass.desc
locale.en: Custom classes for the button, separated by spaces – for individual CSS or for evaluation in scripts. Only letters, digits, hyphen and underscore are allowed.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.buttonAriaLabel.desc
locale.en: Replaces the label announced for the button. Useful when the visible text alone is not meaningful – for example "Learn more" becomes "Learn more about SEO & visibility". Leave empty when the button text is already unambiguous.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.buttonDataAttributes.desc
locale.en: Additional data- attributes on the button, for example for tracking or custom scripts. Names must start with data-.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.imageMaxHeight.desc
locale.en: Limits the height of the images in all cards, for example "320" for 320 pixels. A number without a unit is read as pixels, values like "50vh" or "20rem" work as well. Individual cards can deviate from this. On narrow devices an image is additionally limited to a share of the screen height automatically, so it cannot push the text out of view – a separate value for mobile is therefore not needed.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.imageFit.desc
locale.en: Defines for all cards how the image fills its space. "Fill the area" always covers the space completely and crops the edges – good for photos. "Show completely" scales the image down until all of it is visible – good for logos or graphics. Individual cards can deviate from this.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.imageCrop.desc
locale.en: Which part of the images always stays visible when they get cropped. Only has an effect together with "Fill the area". Individual cards can deviate from this.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.contentSecondary.desc
locale.en: Content of the second text area. This area holds nothing but this content - no number, no headline, no button - which makes it the place for own HTML styled through the brick's own CSS. Note: the two areas only sit side by side within the scroll effect; once the cards appear below each other, this area sits below the first one at full width.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.contentPrimaryPadding
locale.en: Inner spacing of the text area

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.contentPrimaryPadding.desc
locale.en: Space between the text and the edge of the card. "None" lets the content run up to the edge - useful when the area holds own HTML that brings its own spacing. With "Use the global setting" whatever is configured on the brick applies.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.contentSecondaryPadding
locale.en: Inner spacing of the second text area

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.contentSecondaryPadding.desc
locale.en: Space between the content of the second area and the edge of the card. With "Use the global setting" whatever is configured on the brick applies.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.imageVerticalAlign.desc
locale.en: Where the image sits inside its area: top, centred or bottom. Only has an effect when the image does not fill its area - that is with "Show completely" or when a maximum image height is set. With "Fill the area" and no height limit it has no effect; there the image focus decides.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.imagePadding
locale.en: Inner spacing of the image area

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.imagePadding.desc
locale.en: Space between the image and the edge of the card. Without inner spacing the image bleeds into the corners of the card - that is the normal case. Inner spacing pays off for a cut-out motif that should keep the card surface visible around it. With "Use the global setting" whatever is configured on the brick applies.

locale.name: brick.scrollPinnedCards.entries.cardClass.desc
locale.en: Own CSS class for the whole card. It lets the brick's own CSS target this single card - including individual areas inside it, e.g. ".my-class .quiqqer-presentationBricks-scrollPinnedCards__cardBodySecondary". Separate several classes with spaces.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.contentPadding
locale.en: Inner spacing of the text areas (all cards)

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.contentPadding.desc
locale.en: Space between the text and the edge of the card. The value grows with the width of the card and gives way on a short window so the content keeps its room. Individual cards can deviate from this.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.buttonsAligned
locale.en: Buttons of all cards on one line

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.buttonsAligned.desc
locale.en: Moves the button to the lower edge of the card so that the buttons of all cards sit at the same height. The text keeps the vertical alignment it is set to. Only has an effect within the scroll effect - when the cards are stacked there is no free space in the card to distribute.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.imageVerticalAlign
locale.en: Vertical position of the images (all cards)

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.imageVerticalAlign.desc
locale.en: Where the images sit inside their area. Only has an effect when an image does not fill its area - that is with "Show completely" or with a maximum image height set. Individual cards can deviate from this.

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.imagePadding
locale.en: Inner spacing of the image area (all cards)

locale.name: control.ScrollPinnedCards.imagePadding.desc
locale.en: Space between the image and the edge of the card. Without inner spacing the images bleed into the corners of the card. Individual cards can deviate from this.
